#!/bin/sh
# Flux job script translated from Slurm

#flux: --job-name=tools
#flux: -N 1
#flux: -n 1
#flux: -t 01:00:00

# Job output and error will be combined into the same file.
# The Slurm '%j' is replaced with Flux's '{job.id}'.
#flux: -o tools.eo{job.id}

# Echo des commandes
ulimit -c 0
ulimit -s unlimited

# Arrete du job des la premiere erreur
set -e

# Sourcing the environment profile is preserved.
. ~rodierq/DEV_57/MNH-PHYEX070-b95d84d7/conf/profile_mesonh-LXifort-R8I4-MNH-V5-6-2-ECRAD140-MPIAUTO-O2

# The environment variable SRC_MESONH is assumed to be set by the profile sourced above.
ln -sf ${SRC_MESONH}/src/LIB/Python/* .

module purge
module load python/3.7.6

# The commands are run directly, as this is a single-task job.
python3 plot_16JAN.py
convert *.png 16JAN.pdf

issues: The script sources a user-specific, hardcoded path: '. ~rodierq/DEV_57/...'. This makes the script non-portable and it will fail if run by another user or if the directory structure changes. Using environment modules or relative paths is a more robust approach.

The `ln` command relies on the environment variable `$SRC_MESONH` being correctly set by the `profile_mesonh` script that is sourced. This dependency makes the script fragile; if the sourced script changes or fails, this command will also fail.

#!/bin/sh
#SBATCH -J tools
#SBATCH -N 1            # nodes number
#SBATCH -n 1            # CPUs number (on all nodes) 
#SBATCH -o tools.eo%j   #
#SBATCH -e tools.eo%j   #
#SBATCH -t 01:00:00    # time limit
# Echo des commandes
ulimit -c 0
ulimit -s unlimited
# Arrete du job des la premiere erreur
set -e

. ~rodierq/DEV_57/MNH-PHYEX070-b95d84d7/conf/profile_mesonh-LXifort-R8I4-MNH-V5-6-2-ECRAD140-MPIAUTO-O2
